prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the development of long-acting incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity.

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange the committee is unified on B013 as a single achievement and on Drucker and Holst, so the only real decision is the third seat, and that turns on a principle. The principle I hold is that this prize should honour the discovery chain that changed medicine, and that the chain does not end at the hormone. Holst and Drucker established the physiology and the proglucagon-derived peptide biology. The native peptide, however, has a half-life of minutes and is degraded by DPP-4, so it could not have become a therapy. Knudsen's acylated analogues solved that specific, documented obstacle, and liraglutide and semaglutide are the agents behind the glycaemic, weight, cardiovascular and renal outcome data that make the field mature. A citation that names the physiology and the long-acting therapies, limited to established indications in type 2 diabetes and obesity, describes the whole chain accurately. I hold this with moderate confidence, not high.
statement.case_against: Four colleagues, El-Manira, Linnarsson, Sandberg and Svenningsson, prefer Mojsov, and their position is coherent: a discovery-based trio keeps the prize on physiology and peptide identity, and the identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is a real scientific step that my trio omits. The supplied record does not let me verify Mojsov's contested early-1980s priority, so I cannot say she has a weaker claim, only that the record does not settle it. Honouring an industrial drug developer also blurs discovery and product engineering, and Habener, outside the credited names, remains an unresolved gap for either trio. A defensible discovery-only prize for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov would be a legitimate outcome, and a Knudsen trio will be criticised by those who think the peptide identification deserved the seat.

responses.point: Prefers Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, with a citation that includes identification of the active form, and says that if the committee judges drug development indispensable the trio is the wrong one.
responses.response: Your conditional is the right way to frame it, and I think the drug-development step is indispensable to this citation, because the short half-life and DPP-4 degradation are why the native peptide was never a drug. I agree that Mojsov's identification of the active form is a genuine contribution, but your own account and the record leave her priority unverified, so it cannot carry a seat that I would otherwise give to a documented, concrete step. I still prefer Knudsen. I accept that your trio is a defensible discovery-first reading and not an error.

responses.point: Names Mojsov as covering the discovery side of the chain and warns that a prize that includes drug development blurs physiology and industrial optimisation, while also noting unanimity could hide the attribution problem.
responses.response: I take the point that unanimity on B013 can hide the attribution problem, which is why I have tried to settle the seat on a principle and not on counts. I do not think including Knudsen blurs the line badly, because the work is the solution to a specific mechanistic problem, the half-life of the peptide, and not generic drug optimisation. Where I move toward you is on scope: I would keep the citation to physiology and established indications and avoid any wording that implies credit for the later non-metabolic or central-appetite work.

responses.point: As chair, ranks the discovery side first, says a Mojsov trio keeps the award on scientific discovery, and says leaving Knudsen out will be read as favouring discovery over development.
responses.response: I agree with your own concession that leaving Knudsen out will be read as favouring discovery over development, and I think that is a cost of the Mojsov trio, not a neutral outcome. On your question whether Habener's absence undermines either trio, I think it weakens both about equally, since neither trio can claim to have settled the early peptide history from the supplied names. That argues for deciding the seat on the discovery-versus-development principle you posed, and for me that principle favours a chain-based citation. I note we remain 4-2 apart and I do not regard the count as an argument.

responses.point: Proposes Drucker, Holst and Mojsov and treats Knudsen as substantial but industrial, while saying a basic-science trio can be criticised for omitting the people who made the drugs.
responses.response: You name the weakness of each trio fairly, and I agree a trio including Knudsen omits a basic discoverer just as yours omits the drug developer. I moved on one point from round 1: I no longer say I could simply support your trio as a fallback without conditions, because I now think the choice should be made explicitly on the discovery-or-development principle. If the committee settles on discovery only, I would accept Mojsov in that case, but I would not call it the stronger configuration.

responses.point: Shares the Knudsen trio and says that if the committee decides identification of the active peptide outweighs analogue design, Mojsov belongs in it, while admitting the credit history rests on recollection.
responses.response: I agree with your analysis of the chain, and with your candour that the credit history rests on recollection, since that applies to both of us on the Mojsov question. My difference with you is small: you hold the framing with less confidence, whereas I think the DPP-4 and half-life argument gives the Knudsen seat a firmer basis in the record. We both would restrict the citation to established diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal evidence, and I would keep that restriction explicit.

uncertainties: Whether the committee settles the third seat on a discovery-only or a chain-based principle, and whether the 4-2 split on Mojsov versus Knudsen can be resolved from the supplied record.
Mojsov's early-1980s priority over the active peptide and Habener's role remain unverified from the supplied material.
Whether long-term safety and emerging non-metabolic indications should limit the wording of the citation.
If B013 stalls, whether B042 can be framed without Eshhar and with Rosenberg limited to adoptive cell transfer, or whether B010 has a more resolvable trio.
statement.conflict_note: No documented involvement with any credited name on a shortlisted ballot. My field is autoimmunity and rheumatology, so I may weigh B042 too generously and I rely on B013 for that reason, not because of my field. I have no documented personal tie to Drucker, Holst, Knudsen or Mojsov, and shared Karolinska or Bergen affiliations with other researchers do not establish one. Disclosure is unchanged from round 1.
